Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.style

Class LevelConstraint

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.LevelConstraint
public final class LevelConstraint extends Object
The depth(n) / * side of a style declaration or query, encoded as a long bitmask instead of the ad-hoc level/isStared pair the legacy net.sourceforge.plantuml.style.StyleKey carries -- levels are assumed to fit in 0..63, which every real mindmap/wbs diagram does. This class is deliberately used on both sides of a match, exactly like the legacy StyleSignatureBasic is: the very same fields play a different role depending on whether they sit on the declaration or on the query, mirrored here from StyleSignatureBasic#matchAllImpl: 
   if (declaration.hasLevel())
     if (declaration.isStar())
       require query.hasLevel() && query.level >= declaration.level      // "at least"
     else
       require query.hasLevel() && query.level == declaration.level      // exact
   if (query.isStar() && declaration.isStar() == false)
     fail                                                                // star-query gate
On the declaration side: star turns its own level from an exact match into "matches this level or any deeper one" -- this is what a literal depth(3)* selector in a .skin/style file means. On the query side: level is simply "the element being matched sits at this depth", and star means "this is an ancestor-inheritance lookup" (see net.sourceforge.plantuml.mindmap.Idea#getStyle(), which walks ancestors with .addStar()): such a query only ever matches declarations that are themselves star, which is exactly how the old code restricts ancestor inheritance to catch-all (depth(n)*, or plain *) declarations, without needing a separate isStarred flag anywhere else.
